models.name: ecommerce_mall_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors accessing login and registration endpoints.

Guests are temporary browser sessions that allow visitors to access authentication endpoints before registering. Unlike registered customers, sellers, or administrators, guests do not have credentials or persistent identity.

Each guest account can have multiple temporary session tokens stored in the {@link ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions} table. Guest accounts are automatically cleaned up after expiration and do not persist beyond the current browsing session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_guest_sessions
models.description: Guest session tokens tracking JWT authentication sessions for unauthenticated guest visitors. Stores connection metadata (IP, referrer) and session lifecycle timestamps. Belongs to {@link ecommerce_mall_guests}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged guest's {@link ecommerce_mall_guests.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Created at.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expired at.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customers
models.description:
Registered customer accounts with email and password authentication.

This table stores the core identity information for customers who purchase products on the platform. Each customer has exactly one account identified by their email address. The password is stored as a hash for security.

When a customer deletes their account:
- Their profile information in {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_profiles} is deleted
- Their orders and order history are preserved (for seller records and legal purposes)
- Their reviews are preserved but displayed as "deleted user"

Customers authenticate using email and password. Session management is handled in the separate {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions} table, and password reset tokens are stored in {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_password_resets}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Customer's email address used for login and communications. Must be unique across all customers.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for authentication. The actual password is never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer account was soft deleted. Null if account is active. Used for account deletion preservation of orders and reviews.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens tracking customer authentication sessions with access and refresh tokens. Sessions record connection context (IP, headers, referrer) and temporal fields for security auditing. Each customer can have multiple active sessions. Sessions are append-only records that expire according to security policies.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who owns this session. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address from which the session was established.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Page URL where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referer header value indicating the source page that linked to the login endpoint.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Sessions are considered invalid after this time.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for customer password recovery. Each token represents a temporary password reset request linked to a customer account. Tokens expire after a configured duration and are single-use.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token string sent to customer email for verification.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Token expiration timestamp. Tokens become invalid after this time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Token creation timestamp.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller accounts with authentication credentials and approval workflow status.

Sellers are member-type actors who sell products on the platform. Each seller must register with email and password, then obtain administrator approval before listing products. The approval_status field tracks the seller's standing: pending (awaiting approval), approved (can sell), rejected (must reapply), or suspended (administrative action).

Account deletion is soft-deleted via deleted_at and only allowed when no pending orders, cancellations, or refunds exist. When deleted, products are hidden but order history and snapshots are preserved for legal/compliance purposes.

{@link ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions} tracks login sessions.
{@link ecommerce_mall_seller_password_resets} handles password recovery.
{@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations} manages approval workflow with rejection reasons.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for login and account identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Bcrypt hashed password for authentication.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Account approval state: pending, approved, rejected, or suspended. Controls seller's ability to list products.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent account update.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if account is active. Set when seller deletes account (if no pending transactions).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions
models.description: Session records for seller authentication tracking JWT tokens with access and refresh tokens. Each session captures connection context (IP, href, referrer) and temporal boundaries for security auditing. Sessions are append-only records that track login events for compliance and security analysis.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: Client IP address at session creation.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: Request origin URL or referer header.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Full referrer URL from request headers.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp for security.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for seller password recovery.

Stores unique tokens with expiration timestamps that allow sellers to reset their passwords securely. Each token belongs to a specific seller and becomes invalid after the expiration time. Tokens are created when a password reset is requested and deleted after use or expiration. The table supports the authentication recovery workflow by ensuring tokens are unique and time-limited.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token string for authentication recovery.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp when the token becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with authentication credentials and privilege levels.

This table represents administrators who manage the e-commerce platform. Administrators have elevated privileges including approving seller registrations, managing categories, overseeing orders/products, and suspending/banning users.

There are two administrator grades: regular administrators and super administrators. Super administrators can promote/demote other administrators and approve admin promotion requests.

Administrators authenticate using email and password. Session management is handled by {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions}. Password reset tokens are managed by {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_password_resets}. Administrator actions are audited through {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs}.

Account status tracks whether an administrator is active, suspended, or banned. Suspended/banned administrators cannot log in or perform administrative actions.

All administrator data modifications are tracked with snapshots for audit trail purposes.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator's email address used for login. Must be unique across all administrator accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator privilege level. Valid values: 'regular', 'super_admin'. Regular admins can approve sellers, manage categories, and oversee platform. Super admins can additionally promote/demote administrators and approve admin promotion requests.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Account status for login and access control. Valid values: 'active', 'suspended', 'banned'. Only 'active' administrators can log in and perform actions.

plainFields.name: nickname
plainFields.description: Display name or alias for the administrator shown in audit logs and system interfaces. Optional but recommended for identification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the account is considered deleted but preserved for audit trail integrity.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication tracking.

Administrator login sessions are recorded with connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) for security auditing and session lifecycle management. Each session represents a logged-in administrator with an access token that expires for security purposes.

Sessions are append-only and represent a complete authentication audit trail. When an admin logs out or the session expires, the record is preserved for security analysis.

Referenced by: {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}. Links the session to the authenticated admin account.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initiated. Captured for security auditing and anomaly detection.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The full URL of the page where the login was initiated. Used for tracking session origin.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP Referrer header value indicating the previous page before login. Captured for security audit trail.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session token expires. After this time, the session is no longer valid for authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created (login time).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery.

Stores temporary tokens used for administrator password reset flows. Each record represents a single password reset attempt with an expiration timestamp for security. Tokens are automatically invalidated after expiration. Related to the parent administrator via {@link ecommerce_mall_admins}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token sent via email for security verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the password reset token was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: When the password reset token expires and becomes invalid.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_audit_logs
models.description: Audit log table recording all administrator actions for security monitoring and compliance tracking. Each entry captures who performed an action, what action was taken, which resource was affected, and contextual metadata including IP address and user agent for forensic analysis.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the action. References {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action
plainFields.description: The specific action performed by the administrator (e.g., 'approve_seller', 'suspend_user', 'delete_product').

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: The type of resource affected by this action (e.g., 'seller', 'product', 'order', 'user').

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: The unique identifier of the affected resource.

plainFields.name: details
plainFields.description: Additional details about the action in JSON or text format, such as before/after values or reason.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the action was performed for security audit purposes.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the browser/client used for the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_super_admins
models.description:
Super administrator accounts representing the highest privilege level in the platform hierarchy.

Super administrators have elevated privileges including:
- Approving/rejecting administrator promotion requests
- Promoting regular administrators to super administrator
- Demoting super administrators to regular administrator (except themselves)
- Managing the administrator hierarchy and grade levels

Each super admin requires email-based authentication with password login.
Super admin accounts can be soft deleted but historical audit data is preserved.

This table serves as the canonical identity record for super administrators.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Login email address for super administrator authentication. Must be unique across all super admin accounts.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never store plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: grade
plainFields.description: Administrator grade level indicating super administrator status. Fixed value identifying highest privilege tier.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the super administrator account.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Non-null indicates account deletion while preserving audit history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_super_admin_sessions
models.description:
Super administrator session tokens for authentication and session management.

Stores JWT access and refresh tokens along with connection context metadata (IP address, page URL, referrer) for audit and security purposes. Records when the session was established and when it expires.

Belongs to {@link ecommerce_mall_super_admins} and represents active login sessions for super administrators with elevated system privileges.

foreignFields.name: super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged super administrator's {@link ecommerce_mall_super_admins.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the client connecting the session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL from the session initiation request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of the session record.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Expiration time when the session becomes invalid.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_super_admin_password_resets
models.description: Password reset tokens for super administrator accounts. Stores temporary tokens used to verify identity during password recovery workflows. Each token has an expiration time for security and can only be used once.

foreignFields.name: super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Super administrator requesting the password reset. {@link ecommerce_mall_super_admins.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token. Cryptographically secure random string used in password reset links.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset request was created.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token expires and becomes invalid. Set based on security policy (typically 1 hour).

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the token was successfully used to reset the password. Null until consumed.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_super_admin_audit_logs
models.description: Audit log tracking critical security events performed by super administrators. Records all significant actions taken by super admins including administrator promotions/demotions, system-level configuration changes, and sensitive operations. Each entry captures the action type, affected entity, contextual information (IP address, user agent), and timestamp for security auditing and compliance purposes.

foreignFields.name: super_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged super administrator's {@link ecommerce_mall_super_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed (e.g., 'admin_promote', 'admin_demote', 'system_config_change', 'force_action').

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the action performed including relevant context and parameters.

plainFields.name: target_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected by the action (e.g., 'admin', 'seller', 'customer', 'system'). Null for general system actions.

plainFields.name: target_id
plainFields.description: UUID of the affected entity. Null for general system actions or when not applicable.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the action was performed for security tracking.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the browser/client used for the action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshot of product state at time of purchase, preserving name, description, category, and base price for each order item. Created when an order is placed successfully to ensure accurate historical record for dispute resolution and legal compliance. Related to {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items} via 1:1 relationship. Image URLs are stored in a normalized child table.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}. Establishes 1:1 relationship to preserve product state at purchase time.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category reference at time of purchase. {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}. Nullable if category was deleted after purchase.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name at time of purchase. Preserved exactly as displayed to customer during checkout.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Product description at time of purchase. Preserved for historical record and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: category_name
plainFields.description: Category name at time of purchase. Denormalized to preserve category state even if category is later renamed or deleted.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Product base price at time of purchase. Preserved in order currency for accurate pricing history.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when snapshot was created. Immutable record of when the product state was captured.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots capturing product variant state at time of purchase.

Preserves the exact SKU code, option values, and price of a product variant when an order was placed. These snapshots are critical for dispute resolution and serve as legal proof of what variant was actually purchased. Each order item has exactly one corresponding variant snapshot at creation time.

Individual option values (Color, Size, etc.) are stored in the {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshot_attributes} child table to maintain 1NF compliance.

References the order item and provides the complete variant state as it existed at purchase. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items}

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}. Enforces 1:1 relationship - each order item has exactly one variant snapshot.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: SKU code of the variant at time of purchase.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Price per unit of the variant at time of purchase.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created (order placement time).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of seller profile states captured at the time of order purchase.

This table preserves the exact shop name and logo of the seller at the moment an order item was created, ensuring that historical order records remain accurate even if the seller later changes their profile information. This is critical for dispute resolution, legal compliance, and maintaining accurate order history in an e-commerce platform where money is exchanged.

These snapshots are linked to order items via {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items} and cannot be modified or deleted once created. The preserved data includes the seller's public identity information (shop name and logo) that was visible to the customer at the time of purchase.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: The order item this seller snapshot belongs to. References {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}. Captures which specific order line item this seller profile state is associated with.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: The seller's shop name at the time of purchase. Preserved exactly as it appeared when the order was placed, regardless of subsequent changes to the seller's profile.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description: The URL to the seller's shop logo image at the time of purchase. Preserves the visual identity of the seller as it appeared when the order was created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records exactly when the seller profile state was captured during order processing.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshot_images
models.description: Normalized child table storing individual product image URLs for order item product snapshots. Each row represents one image belonging to a specific product snapshot captured at order time, with display ordering to preserve sequence (first image serves as thumbnail/main image). This table ensures 1NF compliance by decomposing the image array into individual atomic records rather than storing as JSON.

foreignFields.name: order_item_product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.id}. Links the image to the specific product snapshot captured at order time.

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: URL or file path to the product image. Captures the image location at the time of order.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display ordering for images within the product snapshot. Lower values appear first. The first image (display_order = 0 or minimum value) serves as the main/thumbnail image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the image snapshot was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshot_attributes
models.description:
Normalized child table storing individual option key-value pairs for product variant snapshots at time of order purchase.

Each row represents one option attribute (e.g., Color: Red, Size: Large) belonging to a specific order item variant snapshot. This table exists to maintain First Normal Form (1NF) compliance by decomposing the variant options data structure into atomic key-value records rather than storing composite data.

The table stores option names (like 'Color', 'Size') and their corresponding values (like 'Red', 'Large') as separate rows linked to the parent variant snapshot. This enables historical preservation of exact variant specifications at order time for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

Each variant snapshot can have multiple attributes. A unique constraint prevents duplicate option keys within the same variant snapshot. Attributes are immutable after creation as part of the immutable snapshot pattern.

foreignFields.name: order_item_variant_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Parent variant snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots.id}. Links this option attribute to the specific variant snapshot it describes.

plainFields.name: option_key
plainFields.description: The option category or attribute name (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'). Represents what characteristic this option describes for the product variant.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: The specific value for this option (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). The actual selection made for the option attribute.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot attribute was created. Part of the immutable snapshot record for audit trail purposes.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_categories
models.description:
Product categories with hierarchical structure supporting one level of nesting (parent/subcategory relationship).

Categories organize products into browsable hierarchies for customer navigation. Each category can optionally have a parent category, creating a two-level hierarchy (top-level categories and subcategories). Categories are managed exclusively by administrators.

When a category is deleted, products in that category become uncategorized but remain in the system. The soft delete pattern preserves category history for existing orders and audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category's {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}. Null for top-level categories.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name displayed to customers. Must be unique within the same parent category.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional category description for display purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if category is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_products
models.description: Main product listings in the e-commerce platform. Each product is owned by a seller and categorized under a specific category. Products serve as the foundation for the catalog, containing basic information like name, description, and base price. The actual purchasable SKUs are managed through child product variants. Products support soft deletion to maintain referential integrity with historical orders while being removable from active listings. Product changes are audited through snapshot records for dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Product owner seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Product category's {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name displayed to customers.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed product description.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Base price of the product. Variant-specific prices can override this.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the product was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the product was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if product is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_images
models.description:
Product images associated with products in the e-commerce platform.

Stores image URLs for each product with display ordering.
The first image in the order serves as the main product thumbnail.
Images can be reordered by updating the display_order field.

Images are managed through their parent product and do not support independent operations.
Changes to images are included in product snapshots for audit trails.

{@link ecommerce_mall_products}

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL to the uploaded product image file.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display ordering index for the image within the product. First image (0) serves as the main thumbnail.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of the record.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time of the record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Deletion timestamp for soft delete. Null if the image is active.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variants
models.description: SKU-level product variants representing specific combinations of product options. Each variant belongs to a product and has a unique SKU code within that product. Variants can have optional price overrides. Stock quantity is tracked separately via inventory_records. When variants are deleted, they are soft-deleted to preserve order history. Individual option values are stored in the normalized ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options child table.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Unique SKU code within the product. Combined with product_id for uniqueness constraint.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Optional variant-specific price that overrides the product's base price. Null when using product's base price.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the variant was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the variant was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if active, set when variant is deleted.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_options
models.description:
Individual option value records for product variants, ensuring 1NF (First Normal Form) compliance by decomposing variant options into atomic key-value pairs.

Each row represents one option type and its corresponding value for a specific product variant (e.g., option_name='Color', option_value='Red'). This normalization enables efficient querying by specific option types (e.g., "find all variants with Color=Red") and eliminates JSON/array storage within string fields.

Related entities:
- Belongs to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants} - each variant can have multiple option records
- Used by {@link ecommerce_mall_cart_items} and {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items} to identify specific variant selections
- Referenced in {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots} to preserve option state at point-in-time

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product variant's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}. Establishes which variant this option value belongs to.

plainFields.name: option_name
plainFields.description: The option type/key (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'). Represents the classification dimension for this option value. Required field - every variant option must have a type name.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: The specific value for this option type (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). Represents the concrete selection value within the option classification. Required field - every variant option must have a value.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp. Automatically set when the option value is first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp. Automatically updated when the option value is modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Customer wishlist entries linking customers to saved products at the product level (not variant level).

This table captures the "save for later" functionality where customers can bookmark products they are interested in purchasing later. Wishlist entries are independent entities managed by customers and can be searched, filtered, and browsed separately from the cart.

When a product is deleted by a seller, wishlist items referencing that product are automatically removed (cascade delete). This table links to {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} for ownership and {@link ecommerce_mall_products} for the saved product reference.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}. References the customer who saved the product to their wishlist.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}. References the product saved in the wishlist.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of the wishlist entry.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time of the wishlist entry. Updated when the entry is modified or accessed.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Customer shopping cart entries linking customers to specific product variants with quantities.

Each cart item represents a product variant that a customer intends to purchase. When a customer adds the same variant to their cart again, quantities are combined rather than creating separate line items. This is enforced by a unique constraint on the customer and variant combination.

Cart items track the desired quantity for each variant. The actual availability and stock status is checked at checkout time, not when adding to cart.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product variant's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of the variant in the cart.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of the cart item.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update time of the cart item.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If set, the cart item is considered removed.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_inventory_records
models.description:
Inventory quantity change records for product variants tracking restocking, order deductions, cancellations, and adjustments.

Each record represents a single inventory movement event - whether stock was added (positive quantity_change) or removed (negative quantity_change). The cumulative sum of all records for a variant represents the current stock level.

Common record types include:
- Restocking: Positive quantity_change when sellers add inventory
- Order deduction: Negative quantity_change when orders are placed
- Cancellation refund: Positive quantity_change when orders are cancelled
- Refund restoration: Positive quantity_change when refunds are processed
- Adjustment: Positive or negative quantity_change for inventory corrections

Records are immutable and serve as an audit trail for inventory management and dispute resolution. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants}

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Target variant's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}.

plainFields.name: quantity_change
plainFields.description: Quantity change amount. Positive values indicate stock increase (restocking, cancellations, refunds). Negative values indicate stock decrease (order placement, adjustments).

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the inventory change. Examples: 'restock', 'order_placed', 'order_cancelled', 'refund_processed', 'inventory_adjustment', 'damaged_goods'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the inventory record was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_orders
models.description: Order headers created when payment succeeds, representing a completed purchase by a customer. Each order tracks the customer who placed it, a unique order number for reference, the total price of all items, and the overall order status derived from its items. The shipping address is stored as a snapshot at order time since customer addresses can be edited or deleted later. Orders support soft deletion to preserve historical transaction records while maintaining data retention policies. Related order items and shipments are managed in separate tables.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who placed the order. References {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Unique order number for customer reference and support inquiries. Format typically includes timestamp and sequence.

plainFields.name: total_price
plainFields.description: Total price of all items in the order, calculated at checkout time.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Overall order status derived from item statuses: paid (all items paid), shipped (any item shipped), delivered (all items delivered), cancelled (all items cancelled), refunded (all items refunded), partially_completed (mixed states).

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Name of the recipient for shipping, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: recipient_phone
plainFields.description: Phone number of the recipient for shipping contact, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: street_address
plainFields.description: Street address line for delivery, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City for delivery, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: state
plainFields.description: State or province for delivery, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal or ZIP code for delivery, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country for delivery, captured from the address at order time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was created (payment succeeded).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if order is active, set when deleted for data retention.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_items
models.description: Individual purchased product variants within an order representing a specific product-variant combination with quantity and price at time of purchase. Each order item tracks its own status lifecycle independently (paid, shipped, delivered, cancelled, refunded), allowing different items within the same order to have different fulfillment states. Order items preserve purchase-time state through separate snapshot tables: {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots}, {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots}, and {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Belongs to order's {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id} containing this item.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belongs to product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id} at time of purchase.

foreignFields.name: variant_id
foreignFields.description: Belongs to product variant's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id} specifying SKU and options.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belongs to seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id} who sold the product variant.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units purchased for this product variant.

plainFields.name: price_at_purchase
plainFields.description: Price per unit at time of purchase (preserved from variant price, allowing for historical accuracy).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current fulfillment status of this order item: 'paid', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled', or 'refunded'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was created (order placed).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the order item was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for when order item is logically deleted (kept for seller records and legal purposes).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipments
models.description:
Packages sent by sellers containing one or more order items from the same seller.

Shipments represent the physical packaging and dispatch of purchased items. Unlike orders which can span multiple sellers,
a shipment always originates from exactly one seller. When a seller prepares to ship items, they group eligible order
items (those with status 'paid') into a single shipment, providing carrier and tracking information.

Key business rules:
- A shipment can contain multiple order items only if they are from the same seller
- Different sellers always ship separately (separate shipments)
- Creating a shipment automatically updates the status of all included order items to 'shipped'
- Customers view shipment tracking information per order to monitor delivery status
- Delivery confirmation is tracked separately via {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_deliveries}
- The order items in a shipment are linked through the junction table {@link ecommerce_mall_shipment_items}

Snapshots are not created for shipments as the tracking information (carrier, number) is immutable once set.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. The seller who created and sent this shipment.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order's {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. The order this shipment fulfills.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of the shipping carrier (e.g., 'FedEx', 'UPS', 'DHL', 'USPS'). Used for tracking and display to customers.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Tracking number provided by the carrier for this shipment. Customers use this to track package delivery status.

plainFields.name: shipped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller marked this shipment as shipped. Used to calculate delivery windows and for order status derivation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Shipments are rarely deleted (only for corrections before delivery), but soft delete is preserved for data integrity.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_items
models.description: Junction table linking order items to shipments, establishing a many-to-many relationship where a single shipment can contain multiple order items. Each order item can only belong to one shipment. This table is automatically managed when sellers create shipments and select items to include.

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent shipment containing this order item. {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item included in this shipment. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this shipment-item association was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_item_snapshots
models.description: Junction table linking order items to their corresponding purchase-time snapshots. When a customer places an order, the system creates snapshots of the product, variant, and seller profile states at that exact moment. This table maintains those relationships, ensuring complete historical preservation of what was purchased from whom and at what price - critical for dispute resolution and legal compliance in an e-commerce platform handling monetary transactions.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Associated product snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_product_snapshots.id}. Captures product name, description, category, and base price at purchase time.

foreignFields.name: variant_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Associated variant snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_variant_snapshots.id}. Captures SKU code, option values, and price at purchase time.

foreignFields.name: seller_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Associated seller snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_item_seller_snapshots.id}. Captures shop name and logo at purchase time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the snapshot relationship was created (when the order was placed).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of entire orders created for audit trails and significant status changes.

References the complete state captured in the parent order table. The shipping_address_id preserves the address reference at the time of snapshot for audit purposes. Snapshots are immutable records that cannot be modified or deleted.

Created automatically when orders undergo significant state changes or when audit records are required for compliance and legal purposes.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order's {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the snapshot was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_deliveries
models.description:
Delivery confirmation records tracking when shipments are delivered and by whom confirmed.

Each shipment has exactly one delivery record created when delivery is confirmed - either manually by the customer or automatically after 14 days. This table preserves the delivery timestamp and confirmation method for audit trails and order status tracking.

Relationships:
- {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments} - The shipment being delivered (1:1)
- {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} - The customer who confirmed delivery (nullable for auto-delivery)

foreignFields.name: shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged shipment's {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who confirmed delivery. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}. Null when automatically delivered by system after 14 days.

plainFields.name: delivered_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shipment was marked as delivered.

plainFields.name: is_auto_delivered
plainFields.description: Whether delivery was automatically confirmed by system after 14-day window (true) or manually confirmed by customer (false).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if not deleted.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests
models.description: Customer cancellation requests for paid-but-unshipped order items. When a customer wants to cancel an order item that has been paid for but not yet shipped, they submit a cancellation request with a reason. The seller then reviews the request and either approves or rejects it. Every approval or rejection creates a snapshot that preserves the state of the request for audit purposes. Cancellation requests preserve the state of the order item and restore stock quantities when approved.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged order item's {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}. The specific order item the customer wants to cancel.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Requesting customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}. The customer who submitted the cancellation request.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Responding seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. The seller who owns the order item and responds to the request. Nullable initially, set when seller reviews.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's reason for requesting cancellation. This explains why the customer wants to cancel the order item.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the cancellation request. Values: 'pending' (awaiting seller response), 'approved' (seller approved, item cancelled), 'rejected' (seller rejected the request).

plainFields.name: response_reason
plainFields.description: Seller's reason for approving or rejecting the cancellation request. Explanation provided when the seller responds to the request.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the request (approved or rejected). Null while status is pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of record.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Update time of record.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Records are soft-deleted per platform data retention policy.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cancellation_request_snapshots
models.description: Immutable point-in-time snapshots of cancellation requests capturing the state before and after approval or rejection events. Each snapshot preserves the complete state of a cancellation request at a specific moment in time, including status transitions and reason changes. Snapshots are append-only and immutable to support audit trails and dispute resolution.

foreignFields.name: cancellation_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged cancellation request's {@link ecommerce_mall_cancellation_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: status_before
plainFields.description: The cancellation request status before the change. Valid values may include 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'cancelled'.

plainFields.name: status_after
plainFields.description: The cancellation request status after the change. Valid values may include 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected', 'cancelled'.

plainFields.name: reason_before
plainFields.description: The cancellation reason provided by the customer before the change, if any.

plainFields.name: reason_after
plainFields.description: The cancellation reason provided by the customer after the change, if any.

plainFields.name: reviewer_note
plainFields.description: Optional note or explanation provided by the seller when approving or rejecting the cancellation request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, capturing the exact moment of the state change.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Customer refund requests for delivered order items within the 7-day return window.

Refund requests are created by customers for order items that have been delivered. Each request tracks the refund reason, current status in the approval workflow, and timestamps for both request creation and seller response. The seller of the product reviews the request and can approve or reject it. When the seller responds, a corresponding snapshot is created in the separate refund_request_snapshots table to preserve the request state and response for audit purposes.

Refund requests maintain the complete lifecycle: pending → approved/rejected. If a request is rejected, the customer may submit a new request within the 7-day window. Approved refunds restore stock quantities via inventory records.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a specific {@link ecommerce_order_items} representing the delivered item
- Created by a {@link ecommerce_mall_customers} customer (the buyer)
- Reviewed by a {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers} seller (the seller of the product)
- Snapshots captured in {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots}

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order item being requested for refund. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer requesting the refund. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who reviews and responds to the refund request. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's explanation for why they are requesting a refund.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request: pending, approved, or rejected.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the refund request.

plainFields.name: responded_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller responded to the refund request. Null if still pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Allows customers to cancel pending refund requests.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_request_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of refund request states captured when a seller responds (approves or rejects). Refund requests allow customers to request refunds for delivered order items within a 7-day window. When a seller reviews and responds to a request, a snapshot is created preserving the complete state including the original reason, status transition, and response reason for audit trails and dispute resolution.

Snapshots are immutable records that serve as legal evidence of the refund request state at the moment of seller response. They cannot be modified or deleted.

foreignFields.name: refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged refund request's {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Customer's refund request reason at the time of snapshot. Preserves the original explanation for why the refund was requested.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Status of the refund request at the time of snapshot. Values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'. Captures the state after seller response.

plainFields.name: response_reason
plainFields.description: Seller's response reason at the time of snapshot. Contains the explanation provided by the seller when approving or rejecting the refund request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created. Records the exact moment the refund request state was preserved for audit purposes.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_reviews
models.description:
Customer reviews and ratings for purchased products.

Reviews represent customer feedback on products they have purchased and received. Each review is linked to a specific order item (purchased variant), and contains a mandatory star rating (1-5) and optional text content. Reviews can only be created after the associated order item has been delivered.

Reviews support edit history through the {@link ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots} table. When a review is edited, a snapshot of the previous state is automatically created. Reviews can be soft-deleted by customers, but snapshots are preserved indefinitely for audit purposes.

Reviews belong to a {@link ecommerce_mall_customers}, a {@link ecommerce_mall_products}, an {@link ecommerce_mall_orders}, and a specific {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items}. The product's average rating is calculated from all non-deleted reviews.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewing customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Reviewed product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Associated order's {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: order_item_id
foreignFields.description: Specific order item (purchased variant) being reviewed. {@link ecommerce_mall_order_items.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Star rating from 1 to 5. Required field representing customer's satisfaction level with the purchased product.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Optional text review content. Free-form customer feedback about their experience with the product.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the review was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp. When set, the review is considered deleted but snapshots are preserved.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshots of review states capturing rating and content at the time of each edit. Created whenever a customer modifies their review to preserve the previous state for audit trails and dispute resolution. Snapshots cannot be modified or deleted.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_review_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged review's {@link ecommerce_mall_reviews.id}.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Rating value (1-5 stars) at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Text content of the review at the time of snapshot. Empty if review had no text content.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the snapshot was created (when the review was edited).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshots of product states capturing the complete product information at a specific point in time. Preserves product name, description, category reference, base price, and associated images for audit trails and dispute resolution. Every edit to a product creates a new snapshot, ensuring historical data integrity for an e-commerce platform handling financial transactions. Snapshots are append-only and cannot be deleted or modified after creation. Related images are stored in {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images}.

foreignFields.name: product_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product's {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}. References the product being snapshotted.

foreignFields.name: category_id
foreignFields.description: Category reference at time of snapshot. Belonged category's {@link ecommerce_mall_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name at the time of snapshot. Preserves the exact product title for historical reference.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Product description at the time of snapshot. Preserves the complete product description text.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Base price of the product at the time of snapshot. Stores the exact price value for historical record.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the snapshot was created. Records the exact moment the snapshot was taken.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of product variant states capturing SKU code and price at a point in time for audit trails and dispute resolution in an e-commerce platform.

Each snapshot represents the complete state of a product variant at a specific moment, preserving historical data even if the parent variant is modified or deleted. Option values are stored in a normalized child table to maintain 1NF compliance.

foreignFields.name: product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product variant being snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: SKU code of the variant at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: price
plainFields.description: Price of the variant at the time of snapshot in decimal format.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Immutable snapshots are append-only.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_profile_snapshots
models.description: Immutable snapshots of seller profile states capturing the complete state of a seller's shop profile at a specific point in time. Each snapshot preserves the shop name, description, and logo image URL as they existed when the snapshot was created. These snapshots serve as an immutable audit trail for dispute resolution, enabling administrators and the platform to review historical states of seller profiles even after subsequent edits or account deletions. Snapshots are created whenever a seller edits their profile content and are referenced by order items to preserve the seller's shop identity at the time of purchase.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller whose profile state is being captured. Links to the seller's identity in {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: shop_name
plainFields.description: The shop name of the seller at the time the snapshot was created. Preserves the exact shop name that was displayed to customers.

plainFields.name: shop_description
plainFields.description: The shop description of the seller at the time the snapshot was created. Preserves the brand representation and store narrative. May be null if no description was set.

plainFields.name: logo_image_url
plainFields.description: The URL of the seller's logo image at the time the snapshot was created. Preserves the visual identity of the shop. May be null if no logo image was set.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created to preserve the seller profile state. Captures the exact moment of the profile edit that triggered this snapshot.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_images
models.description:
Stores images associated with a product snapshot, preserving the image URLs/paths and display order at the time of snapshot.

Each snapshot can have multiple images with ordering where the first image serves as the main/thumbnail. This table enables complete reconstruction of the product's visual presentation at any point in time for dispute resolution and audit purposes.

Images are stored with their display order to maintain the exact presentation sequence that customers would have seen. The first image (order = 1) serves as the thumbnail/main image, while subsequent images provide additional product views.

{@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_snapshots.id}.

plainFields.name: url
plainFields.description: URL or path to the image file stored at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display order of the image within the snapshot. First image (1) is the main/thumbnail image.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When this snapshot image record was created.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_option_values
models.description: Normalized key-value store for product variant snapshot option values. Each row represents a single option key-value pair (e.g., option_name='Color', option_value='Red') belonging to a specific {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots}. This table ensures 1NF compliance by decomposing variant options from JSON/array storage into separate atomic records, enabling efficient filtering and querying by specific option types.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged product variant snapshot's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variant_snapshots.id}.

plainFields.name: option_name
plainFields.description: The name of the option (e.g., 'Color', 'Size', 'Material'). Represents the key in the key-value pair for variant configuration.

plainFields.name: option_value
plainFields.description: The value of the option (e.g., 'Red', 'Large', 'Cotton'). Represents the value in the key-value pair for variant configuration.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation time of the record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations
models.description:
Tracks seller registration applications and their approval workflow status.

Each seller submits a registration application that must be reviewed by an administrator before they can sell products on the platform. The registration records the submission timestamp, current approval status, and if rejected, the reason provided by the reviewing administrator.

Key relationships:
- {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers}: The seller who submitted this registration application
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admins}: The administrator who reviewed and processed the application
- {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_snapshots}: Snapshots capturing state changes for audit trails

The registration flows through three statuses:
- "pending": Application submitted, awaiting administrator review
- "approved": Administrator approved, seller can now list products
- "rejected": Administrator rejected with a provided reason; seller can reapply

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: The {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id} of the seller who submitted this registration application.

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id} of the administrator who reviewed this application. Set when status changes from pending to approved or rejected.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current approval status of the registration application. Values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (seller can sell), 'rejected' (administrator denied, reason provided).

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the administrator when rejecting the application. Only populated when status is 'rejected'. Required for audit and for sellers to understand why their application was denied.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the seller submitted the registration application.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this record, typically when it was reviewed by an administrator.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when an administrator reviewed and processed this application. Set when status changes from pending to approved or rejected.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of seller registration state changes for audit trail and dispute resolution.

This table captures point-in-time records when a seller registration is reviewed by an administrator. Each entry represents a review event, recording which administrator performed the review and when.

Snapshots are append-only and immutable - they can never be deleted or modified once created. They reference the parent {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations.id} table to provide context. The actual registration state (status, rejection_reason) at the time of review is stored in the parent table; this snapshot records the review event metadata (who and when).

For administrators, these snapshots provide a complete audit trail of all review actions performed on registrations.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_registration_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent seller registration that this snapshot belongs to. Links the snapshot to the original registration record in {@link ecommerce_mall_seller_registrations.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who reviewed the registration when this snapshot was created. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Represents the exact moment the review event was recorded for the audit trail.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests
models.description:
Tracks user requests to become administrators and their review workflow status.

This table contains the main entity for administrator promotion requests submitted by customers or sellers who wish to become administrators. Each request includes a reason for the promotion and tracks the review status through the approval workflow.

For polymorphic ownership (requester can be either Customer or Seller), this table uses the main entity + subtype pattern:
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_customers} for customer requests
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_sellers} for seller requests

When a request is approved, the user becomes a regular administrator. When rejected, the rejection reason is recorded in rejection_reason field and the user may submit a new request.

Requests transition through statuses: pending → approved OR pending → rejected.

Related entities:
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_customers} - subtype for customer requests
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_sellers} - subtype for seller requests
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admins} - reviewer who processes the request via reviewer_id
- {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots} - audit trail when status changes occur

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator who reviewed the request. {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the promotion request. Values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Requester's reason for wanting to become an administrator

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the reviewer if the request is rejected. Null if approved or still pending.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: When the promotion request was submitted

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: When the promotion request was last updated

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If set, the record is logically deleted.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable snapshots of admin promotion request state changes for audit trail and dispute resolution.

This table captures the complete state transition of administrator promotion requests whenever their status changes. Each record represents a point-in-time capture of the request at the moment of change, preserving both the previous and new state values along with the reviewer identity.

**Business Context**
Since this platform handles administrative privilege changes, all state modifications must be auditably preserved to support compliance, security reviews, and potential disputes about who was promoted and when.

**Key Relationships**
- Belongs to {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests} - the parent promotion request
- Captures reviewer identity at time of snapshot via {@link ecommerce_mall_admins}
- Referenced only for audit and historical review purposes

**Important Behavioral Notes**
- Appended only when promotion request status changes
- Never updated or deleted (immutable audit trail)
- Each status change creates exactly one snapshot record
- Enables reconstruction of entire request history chronologically

foreignFields.name: admin_promotion_request_id
foreignFields.description: The parent admin promotion request being snapshotted. {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id}

foreignFields.name: previous_reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who last reviewed this request before this change. {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}

foreignFields.name: new_reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who processed this state change (approver/rejecter). {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: The status of the promotion request before this state change. Valid values: 'pending', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The status of the promotion request after this state change. Valid values: 'approved', 'rejected'. Snapshots record transitions to final states.

plainFields.name: previous_reason
plainFields.description: The rejection or approval reason associated with the previous reviewer action, if any. Preserved for complete audit trail.

plainFields.name: new_reason
plainFields.description: The rejection reason provided when rejecting, or the promotion notes when approving. Captures the reviewer's explanation for the state decision.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created (when the promotion request status changed).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_customers
models.description: Polymorphic subtype table linking administrator promotion requests to the requesting customer. Enforces a 1:1 relationship with the parent promotion request entity, ensuring each promotion request is associated with exactly one customer. This table implements the polymorphic ownership pattern where promotion requests can be initiated by either customers or sellers.

foreignFields.name: admin_promotion_request_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged admin promotion request's {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id}. References the parent promotion request entity with 1:1 relationship.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: Requesting customer's {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}. Identifies the customer who submitted the promotion request.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Record last update timestamp.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_request_sellers
models.description: Polymorphic subtype for seller requests to become administrators. Links promotion requests to the requesting seller with unique constraint enforcing 1:1 relationship. When a seller submits a promotion request, this table records the association between the request and the seller's identity.

foreignFields.name: admin_promotion_request_id
foreignFields.description: Linked admin promotion request's {@link ecommerce_mall_admin_promotion_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Requesting seller's {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
